raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

MiniMax-H3's video VAE decodes a request as overlapping spatial tiles over temporal windows and blends them back together. On `main`, base H3 runs one tile per ViT decoder forward at every quality level (only FastH3 stacked its tiles, through `stack_tiling`), and the output chain after the decoder (tile blend + crop + place, temporal window blend into the destination frames, RGB de-normalization + clamp) is a sequence of FP32 aten ops, each a full pass over the frames. On 4x RTX PRO 5000 the decode stage is 3.26 s of a 30 s five-step 768p t2va request.

This PR:

- decodes up to 64 equal-shaped tiles per decoder forward under `quality="lossless"` (the default) and `"high"` on CUDA. Batching changes the GEMM shapes and therefore the output at rounding level, so it belongs to the lossless tier like the existing fused QK RMSNorm+RoPE;
- replaces the temporal blend write and the de-normalization with JIT kernels that reproduce the eager arithmetic bit-exactly and verify that on first use, so they are not tied to a quality level and run at every level, `exact` included. The tile blend + crop + place stays eager: a kernel for it needs the tiles as one tensor, which neither the one-tile-per-forward decode nor the parallel-tiled decode (whose all-gather hands back rank-interleaved views) provides without a copy, and it is worth under 1 ms per request where it would apply.

## Modifications

Decoder batching (`minimax_h3_video_vae/klvae.py`, `batching.py`, `configs/models/vaes/minimax_h3_video.py`, `configs/pipeline_configs/minimax_h3.py`):

- `MiniMaxH3VideoVAEConfig.decoder_tile_batch` (tiles per decoder forward, default 64, 0 = all of a rank's tiles) and `window_batch` (temporal windows per forward, default 1) replace `stack_tiling`. `_run_tile_tasks` has one path through `batching.forward_many`; width 1 is the released recipe, so `exact` decodes exactly as before. The caps apply only while the VAE's `VaeFastPathGate` is enabled, through the decode stage's existing `use_vae_fast_path(vae, quality_allows(quality, "lossless"))`. No new flag or environment variable.
- `MiniMaxH3VideoVAE` creates the gate; the CUDA installer `maybe_optimize_minimax_h3_vae` registers it, hangs the fused QK RMSNorm+RoPE / cuDNN SDPA attention on it and logs the caps once. Other platforms keep one tile per forward, as on `main`.
- FastH3 sets `decoder_tile_batch = 0`, its previous all-tiles recipe, under `lossless`; its `exact` level now decodes tile by tile like base H3. `--performance-mode memory` resets both caps to 1 at every level. `window_batch` stays at 1: pooling every window into one forward measured 8% slower with a 70.2 GB peak (+10 GB) on the PCIe SM120 box (previous revision of this branch).

Output kernels (`kernels/jit/csrc/diffusion/minimax_h3_vae_output.cuh`, `kernels/ops/diffusion/layout/minimax_h3_vae_output_jit.py`, SM100+):

- `minimax_h3_vae_temporal_blend_write` (temporal ramp blend written straight into the destination frames) and `minimax_h3_vae_denorm_clamp` (RGB de-normalization + clamp, with an in-place mode `out=value` for the frames the decode stage owns, so no second copy of the video is kept). Every step spells the aten arithmetic with explicit round-to-nearest intrinsics (one rounding per op, ramp weights as `k * rcp(n)`), so `torch.equal` holds against the eager chain on both the strided and the 128-bit path.
- Each site sits behind a module-level `BitExactFusionGate`: on first use it compares against the eager result, and a mismatch drops the kernel for the process. The blend site verifies per signature (with and without a previous window, so a plain copy cannot vouch for the blend arithmetic); the de-normalization verifies one probe frame. `is_cuda_sm_at_least` in `kernels/ops/diffusion/common/platform.py` keeps ROCm's gfx-derived capability out of the SM check.

Docs: cookbook quality-level descriptions, FastH3 paragraph and deployment-details bullet; `fused_kernels.mdx`; kernels README; `existing-fast-paths.md`; performance skill.

Tests:

- `multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_minimax_h3_vae_fast_path.py` (CPU, 25 cases): batch partitioning and window iteration, the caps reach the VAE only while the gate is on, the real installer shares one gate between attention and batching, batched decode matches tile-by-tile decode with the expected batch widths, first-use verification and fallback of each output site, in-place de-normalization only on owned frames. `test_server_args.py`: memory mode keeps one tile per forward for H3 and FastH3.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_minimax_h3_vae_output.py`: `torch.equal` against the eager chain over blend extents, strided layouts and the in-place mode; alias and input rejections. `test_model_fast_paths.py`: temporal blend bit-exact and verified per signature; batched decode within 1e-3 of tile-by-tile with the expected batch widths on any CUDA GPU; `revert_tensor` bit-exact, in place only on owned frames.
- `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/diffusion/bench_minimax_h3_vae_output.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

4x RTX PRO 5000 72 GB (SM120), cookbook TP2 + Ulysses2 recipe, t2va 768p 16:9 5 s, 5 steps, seed 1101. The reference is `main` (62cee1b15c, the rebase base) at the same quality level, so the DiT trajectory is identical and only the VAE differs. At 1344x768 the decoder splits each frame into a 4x7 = 28-tile grid over the 4 decode ranks, so under `lossless` each rank decodes its 7 tiles in one forward per temporal window. Frame PSNR / SSIM by ffmpeg on the decoded frames; audio compared as a hash of the decoded stream.

| Request | vs `main` at the same level | Audio |
|---|---|---|
| `exact` | bit-identical frames, 3 runs (both output kernels in the loop) | identical |
| `lossless`, 7 tiles per forward per rank | worst frame 52.1 dB, mean 52.6 dB, SSIM min 0.995 | identical |

The lossless difference is the batching alone: on the previous revision of this branch (whose lossless decode is bit-identical to this head on t2va), one tile per forward with the output kernels kept gave frames and audio bit-identical to `main`'s lossless. No run on this head logged a first-use fallback. The branch was first measured against 57db5089c2 and re-measured after the rebase: `main`'s `lossless` decode and this PR's `lossless` output are bit-identical across the two bases, while `main`'s `exact` decode changed in #44690 (it dropped the Triton QK RMSNorm+RoPE the ViT attention ran at every level), and this PR's `exact` follows it bit for bit on both. On fl2va (first-frame conditioning) the previous revision measured a worst frame of 44.2 dB, mean 45.2 dB, SSIM min 0.986 and identical audio against `main` lossless; that clip differs more for the VAE on its own.

Tests on SM120: `test_minimax_h3_vae_output.py` + `test_model_fast_paths.py -k "minimax_h3 or h3_vae"`, 21 passed. The MiniMax-H3 and VAE unit files pass on CPU (379 cases; the four `test_fasth3_selects_vsa_h3_for_the_transformer` subtests fail on `main` as well on this host).

CI exposure: the H100 cases that keep goldens pin `quality="exact"` in memory mode, where the decode is unchanged; the 4-GPU H100 cases run at the default level without a golden. `minimax_h3_t2va_consumer_budget_1gpu_5090` (SM120, memory mode, pinned `exact`) is the one golden case that exercises the temporal blend and de-normalization kernels; their first-use check adds a one-window reference and a one-frame probe inside its 12 GiB cap. The kernel tests run on the `4-gpu-b200` kernel-unit lane: `test_minimax_h3_vae_output.py` is new there, and `test_model_fast_paths.py` gains a second registration on that lane (est. 120 s) because its MiniMax-H3 section needs SM100+, which also gives the file's other sections their first B200 run. This PR's CI is the kernels' first run on SM100; a first-use mismatch there would drop a kernel for the process rather than change output.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

4x RTX PRO 5000 72 GB (SM120, PCIe), torch 2.14.1+cu130, CUDA 13.0, sgl-kernel 0.4.9, flashinfer 0.7.1, driver 580.178.04; base `main` 62cee1b15c. `sglang generate` with `--tp-size 2 --ulysses-degree 2 --encoder-parallel auto --performance-mode speed`, t2va 768p 16:9 5 s, 5 steps (the VAE time does not depend on the step count), one timed request per fresh process after two warmup steps, configurations interleaved in blocks, `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1`. Decode = `MiniMaxH3DecodingStage` duration from `perf_dump.json`; peak = runtime peak reserved.

| | decode ms, median (min–max) | vs `main` same level | peak reserved |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `main`, `exact` | 3404 (3402–3406), n=3 | | 58120 MB |
| this PR, `exact` | 3400 (3391–3409), n=3 | within noise | 58120 MB |
| `main`, `lossless` | 3258 (3252–3264), n=2 | | 58120 MB |
| this PR, `lossless` | 3158 (3147–3162), n=3 | −3.1% | 58120 MB |

On the previous revision of this branch (on 57db5089c2, where `main`'s `lossless` decode measured 3262 (3258–3264), n=7), the output kernels alone (one tile per forward; that revision still fused the tile assembly as well) saved 11 ms (0.3%; 3251 vs 3262 ms, n=2); the rest is the tile batching. The fl2va request showed a similar −3.4% there. End to end, the five-step request stays at 30.2 s; the decode is a tenth of it.

Kernel microbenchmarks (`bench_minimax_h3_vae_output.py`, one SM120 GPU, 448x448 frames):

| op | frames | eager µs | JIT µs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| temporal_blend_write | 17 | 129.8 | 81.2 |
| temporal_blend_write | 33 | 293.4 | 150.9 |
| denorm_clamp | 17 | 80.5 | 37.1 |
| denorm_clamp | 33 | 299.1 | 140.8 |

Not measured on H100/H200 (where only the batching applies) or on SM100/SM103. The benchmark file is registered on the `1-gpu-large` lane, where every SM100+ row skips.

+"""MiniMax-H3 VAE output ops: temporal window write, RGB de-normalization.
+
+Two bit-exact (``torch.equal``) replacements for the eager chain in
+``minimax_h3_video_vae/klvae.py`` and ``processor.py``:
+
+- ``minimax_h3_vae_temporal_blend_write(part, overlap, blend_extent=, out=, start=, count=)``:
+  ``out[:, :, start:start+count]`` receives ``part`` with its first
+  ``blend_extent`` frames blended against the trailing frames of ``overlap``
+  (``None`` disables the blend); the rest of ``out`` is untouched. ``out`` must
+  not alias what is read: the predicate rejects shared storage, the launcher
+  rejects any overlap between the byte range of the written frames and the
+  byte ranges of the frames it reads (a bounds check, so interleaved views of
+  one buffer are rejected too).
+- ``minimax_h3_vae_denorm_clamp(value, mean=, std=, out=None)``:
+  ``clamp((value - mean[c]) / std[c], 0, 1)`` on ``[B, 3, T, H, W]``, NaN
+  preserved; ``out=value`` rewrites a contiguous input in place.
+
+The blend is klvae's linear ramp ``a * (1 - w) + b * w`` with the weight
+``w = k * (1 / n)`` rounded the way aten evaluates ``positions / extent`` for
+a Python-int divisor (reciprocal first), the de-normalization is
+``(x - mean) / std`` as two roundings, and every op is one fp32 rounding, so
+the kernels match eager bit for bit on both the strided and the 128-bit
+vectorized path. The interface carries no H3 constants, but only the
+MiniMax-H3 VAE is wired to it today. SM100+.
+
+Verified on SM120 (RTX PRO 5000): the zero-extent, strided and in-place cases
+in ``test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_minimax_h3_vae_output.py``,
+the 16x16 windows of the MiniMax-H3 section in ``test_model_fast_paths.py``,
+and the first-use ``torch.equal`` check on 1344x768 windows in end-to-end
+decodes; the same tests are registered on the B200 CI lane.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Sequence
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.jit.utils import cache_once, load_jit, make_cpp_args
+from sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion.common.platform import is_cuda_sm_at_least
+from sglang.srt.utils.custom_op import register_custom_op
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from tvm_ffi.module import Module
+
+_MIN_SM = (10, 0)
+# Must match kVecWidth / kVecAlignment in csrc/diffusion/minimax_h3_vae_output.cuh.
+_VEC_WIDTH = 4
+_VEC_ALIGNMENT = 16
+
+
+@cache_once
+def _jit_minimax_h3_vae_output_module(vectorized: bool) -> Module:
+    args = make_cpp_args(vectorized)
+    return load_jit(
+        "diffusion_minimax_h3_vae_output",
+        *args,
+        cuda_files=["diffusion/minimax_h3_vae_output.cuh"],
+        cuda_wrappers=[
+            (
+                "temporal_blend_write",
+                f"minimax_h3_vae_output::TemporalBlendWriteKernel<{args}>::run",
+            ),
+            (
+                "denorm_clamp",
+                f"minimax_h3_vae_output::DenormClampKernel<{args}>::run",
+            ),
+        ],
+    )
+
+
+def _vectorizable(*tensors: torch.Tensor) -> bool:
+    # Mirror of the launcher's 128-bit precondition: innermost stride 1,
+    # `W % 4 == 0`, every other stride and the data pointer 16-byte aligned.
+    return all(
+        t.stride(-1) == 1
+        and t.shape[-1] % _VEC_WIDTH == 0
+        and all(s % _VEC_WIDTH == 0 for s in t.stride()[:-1])
+        and t.data_ptr() % _VEC_ALIGNMENT == 0
+        for t in tensors
+    )
+
+
+@register_custom_op(
+    op_name="diffusion_minimax_h3_vae_temporal_blend_write", mutates_args=["out"]
+)
+def _temporal_blend_write_out(
+    part: torch.Tensor,
+    overlap: torch.Tensor,
+    out: torch.Tensor,
+    start: int,
+    count: int,
+    blend_extent: int,
+    vectorized: bool,
+) -> None:
+    module = _jit_minimax_h3_vae_output_module(vectorized)
+    module.temporal_blend_write(part, overlap, out, start, count, blend_extent)
+
+
+@register_custom_op(
+    op_name="diffusion_minimax_h3_vae_denorm_clamp", mutates_args=["out"]
+)
+def _denorm_clamp_out(
+    value: torch.Tensor,
+    out: torch.Tensor,
+    mean0: float,
+    mean1: float,
+    mean2: float,
+    std0: float,
+    std1: float,
+    std2: float,
+    vectorized: bool,
+) -> None:
+    module = _jit_minimax_h3_vae_output_module(vectorized)
+    module.denorm_clamp(value, out, mean0, mean1, mean2, std0, std1, std2)
+
+
+def minimax_h3_vae_output_device_supported(device: torch.device | int) -> bool:
+    """Whether ``device`` can run these kernels at all (CUDA SM100 or newer);
+    the ``can_use_*`` predicates check the tensors on top of this."""
+    return is_cuda_sm_at_least(_MIN_SM, device)
+
+
+def minimax_h3_vae_temporal_blend_write(
+    part: torch.Tensor,
+    overlap: torch.Tensor | None,
+    *,
+    blend_extent: int,
+    out: torch.Tensor,
+    start: int,
+    count: int,
+) -> None:
+    """Write ``part[:, :, :count]`` into ``out[:, :, start:start+count]``, blending
+    its leading frames against ``overlap`` when one is given."""
+    if overlap is None:
+        # The launcher never reads `overlap` at extent 0; pass `part` for the shape check.
+        overlap, extent = part, 0
+    else:
+        extent = min(int(blend_extent), overlap.shape[2], part.shape[2])
+    _temporal_blend_write_out(
+        part,
+        overlap,
+        out,
+        int(start),
+        int(count),
+        extent,
+        _vectorizable(part, overlap, out),
+    )
+
+
+def can_use_minimax_h3_vae_temporal_blend_write(
+    part: torch.Tensor,
+    overlap: torch.Tensor | None,
+    *,
+    blend_extent: int,
+    out: torch.Tensor,
+    start: int,
+    count: int,
+) -> bool:
+    if not isinstance(part, torch.Tensor):
+        return False
+    tensors = (part, out) if overlap is None else (part, overlap, out)
+    if not all(
+        isinstance(t, torch.Tensor)
+        and t.is_cuda
+        and t.dtype == torch.float32
+        and t.ndim == 5
+        and t.device == part.device
+        and t.shape[:2] == part.shape[:2]
+        and t.shape[3:] == part.shape[3:]
+        for t in tensors
+    ):
+        return False
+    if not (
+        blend_extent >= 0
+        and 0 <= count <= part.shape[2]
+        and start >= 0
+        and start + count <= out.shape[2]
+    ):
+        return False
+    out_storage = out.untyped_storage().data_ptr()
+    if any(t.untyped_storage().data_ptr() == out_storage for t in tensors[:-1]):
+        return False
+    return (
+        is_cuda_sm_at_least(_MIN_SM, part.device) and not torch.compiler.is_compiling()
+    )
+
+
+def minimax_h3_vae_denorm_clamp(
+    value: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    mean: Sequence[float],
+    std: Sequence[float],
+    out: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """``clamp((value - mean[c]) / std[c], 0, 1)`` as one launch; NaN preserved.
+
+    ``out`` is either None (a fresh contiguous buffer) or ``value`` itself,
+    which rewrites a contiguous input in place.
+    """
+    mean = [float(v) for v in mean]
+    std = [float(v) for v in std]
+    if len(mean) != 3 or len(std) != 3:
+        raise ValueError("mean and std must hold one value per RGB channel")
+    if out is None:
+        out = torch.empty(value.shape, dtype=torch.float32, device=value.device)
+    elif out is not value:
+        raise ValueError("out must be None or the input tensor itself")
+    _denorm_clamp_out(value, out, *mean, *std, _vectorizable(value, out))
+    return out
+
+
+def can_use_minimax_h3_vae_denorm_clamp(
+    value: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    mean: Sequence[float],
+    std: Sequence[float],
+    out: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+) -> bool:
+    return (
+        isinstance(value, torch.Tensor)
+        and value.is_cuda
+        and value.dtype == torch.float32
+        and value.ndim == 5
+        and value.shape[1] == 3
+        and value.numel() > 0
+        and (out is None or (out is value and value.is_contiguous()))
+        and len(mean) == 3
+        and len(std) == 3
+        and is_cuda_sm_at_least(_MIN_SM, value.device)
+        and not torch.compiler.is_compiling()
+    )
+
+
+__all__ = [
+    "can_use_minimax_h3_vae_denorm_clamp",
+    "can_use_minimax_h3_vae_temporal_blend_write",
+    "minimax_h3_vae_denorm_clamp",
+    "minimax_h3_vae_output_device_supported",
+    "minimax_h3_vae_temporal_blend_write",
+]

+        raise ValueError("Batch capacity must be positive")

+        while stop < len(values) and stop - start < width:
+            value = values[stop]
+            if (value.shape, value.dtype, value.device) != key:
+                break
+            stop += 1

+        start = stop

+"""MiniMax-H3 VAE output ops (JIT CUDA) vs the eager klvae chain.
+
+One 448x448 frame stack per row: the temporal blend-write of one decoded
+window, and the RGB de-normalization.
+The eager side reuses cached ramp weights, as the production VAE does.
+"""
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.jit.benchmark import marker
+from sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion import (
+    minimax_h3_vae_denorm_clamp,
+    minimax_h3_vae_temporal_blend_write,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion.common.platform import is_cuda_sm_at_least
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(
+    est_time=15, stage="base-b-kernel-benchmark", runner_config="1-gpu-large"
+)
+
+FRAME = 448
+FRAME_OVERLAP = 4
+IMAGENET_MEAN = (-0.485 / 0.229, -0.456 / 0.224, -0.406 / 0.225)
+IMAGENET_STD = (1 / 0.229, 1 / 0.224, 1 / 0.225)
+
+
+def ramp_weights(extent: int):
+    positions = torch.arange(extent, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+    return 1 - positions / extent, positions / extent
+
+
+def eager_blend(a, b, extent, dim, weights):
+    weight_a, weight_b = weights
+    shape = [1] * a.ndim
+    shape[dim] = extent
+    blended = a.narrow(dim, a.shape[dim] - extent, extent) * weight_a.view(shape)
+    blended.add_(b.narrow(dim, 0, extent) * weight_b.view(shape))
+    return torch.cat((blended, b.narrow(dim, extent, b.shape[dim] - extent)), dim=dim)
+
+
+def make_eager_temporal(weights):
+    def fn(part, overlap, out):
+        out[:, :, : part.shape[2]].copy_(
+            eager_blend(overlap, part, FRAME_OVERLAP, 2, weights)
+        )
+
+    return fn
+
+
+def jit_temporal(part, overlap, out):
+    minimax_h3_vae_temporal_blend_write(
+        part,
+        overlap,
+        blend_extent=FRAME_OVERLAP,
+        out=out,
+        start=0,
+        count=part.shape[2],
+    )
+
+
+def make_eager_denorm():
+    mean = torch.tensor(IMAGENET_MEAN, device="cuda").view(1, 3, 1, 1, 1)
+    std = torch.tensor(IMAGENET_STD, device="cuda").view(1, 3, 1, 1, 1)
+
+    def fn(value):
+        return (value - mean).div_(std).clamp_(0, 1)
+
+    return fn
+
+
+def jit_denorm(value):
+    return minimax_h3_vae_denorm_clamp(value, mean=IMAGENET_MEAN, std=IMAGENET_STD)
+
+
+@marker.parametrize("op", ["temporal_blend_write", "denorm_clamp"])
+@marker.parametrize("frames", [17, 33], [17])
+@marker.benchmark("impl", ["eager", "jit"])
+def benchmark(op: str, frames: int, impl: str):
+    if not is_cuda_sm_at_least((10, 0)):
+        marker.skip("MiniMax-H3 VAE output kernels are gated to SM100+")
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(frames)
+    if op == "temporal_blend_write":
+        part = torch.randn(
+            1, 3, frames, FRAME, FRAME, device="cuda", generator=generator
+        )
+        overlap = torch.randn(
+            1, 3, FRAME_OVERLAP, FRAME, FRAME, device="cuda", generator=generator
+        )
+        out = torch.empty_like(part)
+        fn = (
+            make_eager_temporal(ramp_weights(FRAME_OVERLAP))
+            if impl == "eager"
+            else jit_temporal
+        )
+        # In place: `out` is the written tensor, so count it explicitly.
+        return marker.do_bench(
+            fn, input_args=(part, overlap, out), memory_output=(out,)
+        )
+    value = torch.randn(1, 3, frames, FRAME, FRAME, device="cuda", generator=generator)
+    fn = make_eager_denorm() if impl == "eager" else jit_denorm
+    return marker.do_bench(fn, input_args=(value,))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    benchmark.run()

+"""MiniMax-H3 VAE output ops (JIT CUDA) against the eager klvae chain, bitwise.
+
+``blend`` below re-implements ``AutoencoderKL.blend`` with plain aten ops,
+``revert_reference`` the ``VAEProcessor.revert_tensor`` Normalize + clamp.
+Every kernel result must be ``torch.equal`` to its reference (NaN-aware only
+where the input carries NaN); a tolerance here would hide a real bug.
+"""
+
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion import (
+    can_use_minimax_h3_vae_denorm_clamp,
+    can_use_minimax_h3_vae_temporal_blend_write,
+    minimax_h3_vae_denorm_clamp,
+    minimax_h3_vae_temporal_blend_write,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion.common.platform import is_cuda_sm_at_least
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=40, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="4-gpu-b200")
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not is_cuda_sm_at_least((10, 0)),
+    reason="MiniMax-H3 VAE output kernels are gated to SM100+",
+)
+
+IMAGENET_MEAN = (-0.485 / 0.229, -0.456 / 0.224, -0.406 / 0.225)
+IMAGENET_STD = (1 / 0.229, 1 / 0.224, 1 / 0.225)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def inference():
+    torch.manual_seed(20260919)
+    with torch.inference_mode():
+        yield
+
+
+def blend(a, b, extent, dim):
+    # AutoencoderKL.blend: fp32 ramp weights, a * (1 - w) then += b * w.
+    extent = min(a.shape[dim], b.shape[dim], extent)
+    positions = torch.arange(extent, device=b.device, dtype=b.dtype)
+    shape = [1] * a.ndim
+    shape[dim] = extent
+    weight_a = (1 - positions / extent).view(shape)
+    weight_b = (positions / extent).view(shape)
+    blended = a.narrow(dim, a.shape[dim] - extent, extent) * weight_a
+    blended.add_(b.narrow(dim, 0, extent) * weight_b)
+    return torch.cat((blended, b.narrow(dim, extent, b.shape[dim] - extent)), dim=dim)
+
+
+def revert_reference(value, mean, std):
+    mean = value.new_tensor(mean).view(1, 3, 1, 1, 1)
+    std = value.new_tensor(std).view(1, 3, 1, 1, 1)
+    return (value - mean).div_(std).clamp_(0, 1)
+
+
+def assert_bitwise(actual, expected):
+    assert actual.shape == expected.shape and actual.dtype == expected.dtype
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0, equal_nan=True)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("strided", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("extent,count", [(0, 4), (2, 4), (7, 4), (2, 0)])
+def test_temporal_blend_write_matches_eager(strided, extent, count):
+    width = 24 if strided else 12
+    part = torch.randn(2, 3, 5, 8, width, device="cuda")
+    overlap = torch.randn(2, 3, 3, 8, width, device="cuda")
+    storage = torch.full((2, 3, 12, 8, width), -111.0, device="cuda")
+    out = storage

+        part, overlap, blend_extent=extent, out=out, start=3, count=count
+    )
+    expected = out.clone()
+    expected[:, :, 3 : 3 + count] = blend(overlap, part, extent, 2)[:, :, :count]
+    minimax_h3_vae_temporal_blend_write(
+        part, overlap, blend_extent=extent, out=out, start=3, count=count
+    )

+
+
+def test_temporal_blend_write_without_overlap_and_alias_guard():
+    part = torch.randn(1, 3, 5, 7, 11, device="cuda")
+    out = torch.full((1, 3, 8, 7, 11), -9.0, device="cuda")

+        part, None, blend_extent=4, out=out, start=2, count=5
+    )
+    minimax_h3_vae_temporal_blend_write(
+        part, None, blend_extent=4, out=out, start=2, count=5
+    )
+    assert torch.equal(out[:, :, 2:7], part)
+    assert (
+        torch.all(out[:, :, :2] == -9).item() and torch.all(out[:, :, 7:] == -9).item()
+    )
+    # Shared storage is rejected by the predicate, and by the launcher whenever
+    # the byte range of the written frames meets the byte range of the frames
+    # it reads (a bounds check, so interleaved views are rejected as well).
+    assert not can_use_minimax_h3_vae_temporal_blend_write(
+        out[:, :, :5], None, blend_extent=0, out=out, start=0, count=5
+    )
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="alias"):
+        minimax_h3_vae_temporal_blend_write(

+    # in memory (B = C = 1), disjoint frame windows of one buffer are allowed.
+    single = torch.full((1, 1, 8, 7, 11), -9.0, device="cuda")
+    single[:, :, :3] = torch.randn(1, 1, 3, 7, 11, device="cuda")
+    minimax_h3_vae_temporal_blend_write(
+        single[:, :, :3], None, blend_extent=0, out=single, start=5, count=3
+    )
+    assert torch.equal(single[:, :, 5:8], single[:, :, :3])
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="count"):
+        minimax_h3_vae_temporal_blend_write(
+            part, None, blend_extent=0, out=out, start=0, count=6
+        )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("strided", [False, True])
+def test_denorm_clamp_matches_eager(strided):
+    value = torch.randn(2, 3, 5, 8, 24 if strided else 12, device="cuda")
+    if strided:
+        value = value[..., 1::2]
+    value[0, 0, 0, 0, :3] = torch.tensor(
+        [float("nan"), float("inf"), -float("inf")], device="cuda"
+    )
+    assert can_use_minimax_h3_vae_denorm_clamp(
+        value, mean=IMAGENET_MEAN, std=IMAGENET_STD
+    )
+    expected = revert_reference(value, IMAGENET_MEAN, IMAGENET_STD)
+    actual = minimax_h3_vae_denorm_clamp(value, mean=IMAGENET_MEAN, std=IMAGENET_STD)
+    assert actual.is_contiguous()
+    assert_bitwise(actual, expected)
+    assert torch.isnan(actual[0, 0, 0, 0, 0]).item()
+    assert actual[0, 0, 0, 0, 1].item() == 1.0 and actual[0, 0, 0, 0, 2].item() == 0.0
+
+
+def test_denorm_clamp_in_place_rewrites_a_contiguous_input():
+    value = torch.randn(2, 3, 5, 8, 12, device="cuda")
+    expected = revert_reference(value, IMAGENET_MEAN, IMAGENET_STD)
+    assert can_use_minimax_h3_vae_denorm_clamp(
+        value, mean=IMAGENET_MEAN, std=IMAGENET_STD, out=value
+    )
+    actual = minimax_h3_vae_denorm_clamp(
+        value, mean=IMAGENET_MEAN, std=IMAGENET_STD, out=value
+    )
+    assert actual is value
+    assert_bitwise(actual, expected)
+    # Only the input itself may be the output, and only when it is contiguous.
+    strided = torch.randn(2, 3, 5, 8, 24, device="cuda")[..., ::2]
+    assert not can_use_minimax_h3_vae_denorm_clamp(
+        strided, mean=IMAGENET_MEAN, std=IMAGENET_STD, out=strided
+    )
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
+        minimax_h3_vae_denorm_clamp(
+            strided, mean=IMAGENET_MEAN, std=IMAGENET_STD, out=strided
+        )
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        minimax_h3_vae_denorm_clamp(
+            value, mean=IMAGENET_MEAN, std=IMAGENET_STD, out=torch.empty_like(value)
+        )
+
+
+def test_denorm_clamp_rejects_unsupported_inputs():
+    value = torch.randn(2, 4, 5, 8, 12, device="cuda")
+    assert not can_use_minimax_h3_vae_denorm_clamp(
+        value, mean=IMAGENET_MEAN, std=IMAGENET_STD
+    )
+    assert not can_use_minimax_h3_vae_denorm_clamp(
+        value[:, :3].half(), mean=IMAGENET_MEAN, std=IMAGENET_STD
+    )
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
+        minimax_h3_vae_denorm_clamp(value, mean=IMAGENET_MEAN, std=IMAGENET_STD)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))
